lesson.menu_title: Verbs That Commit -- Gerunds and Infinitives in Legal Recommendations, Risk Communication and Professional Decision-Making
lesson.menu_desc: Why "we recommend restructuring" is advice and "we recommend the client to restructure" is not English: the four verb groups, the pairs where the form changes the fact, and a full restructuring recommendation delivered live -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- Verbs That Commit
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leonardo Constantino | Lesson 10 -- Gerunds and Infinitives
lesson.grammar_point: gerunds and infinitives (verb patterns: gerund-only, infinitive-only, both, and meaning change)

listenings.text: Leonardo, this is Ingrid Halvorsen, group general counsel at Vantara. I have read the briefing your team sent last night, and I want to be useful before Thursday rather than after it. Three things. First, the board is not going to reopen the decision to move the reinsurance arm. That is settled, so please avoid spending any part of the call defending it. Second, when you recommend interposing the holding entity, I need you to say what the group is giving up, not only what it is gaining. My chairman will ask, and if he hears only the upside he stops listening. Third, and this is the one that worries me. Somebody in finance is still pushing to opt out of the special regime this year, and I cannot manage to close that conversation on my own. If we opt out first, tell them plainly what we risk losing, and tell them how long an appeal takes. Do not soften it. And please stop sending me eleven pages. Send me one.

I want to tell you about two words that look the same in a memo and are not. Recommend, and advise. Every junior lawyer I have trained writes we recommend the client to restructure, and every one of them is surprised when I cross it out. Recommend does not take a person and an infinitive. You recommend restructuring, or you recommend that the client restructure. Advise does take a person: we advise the client to restructure. It is a small thing, and it is exactly the kind of small thing an English-speaking counterparty notices in the first paragraph. But here is the part that actually matters, and it is not grammar. The verb you choose tells the reader how much of the risk you are carrying. Suggest is soft. Recommend commits you. Advise commits you and names the person who has to act. So before you write the sentence, decide how much you are willing to own. Then pick the verb, and let the pattern follow. I have watched good lawyers spend a year avoiding the strong verb because they were not sure of the form. Learn the form once, and stop paying for it in every memo.

reading.rtitle: Client Briefing -- Vantara Seguros · ALMA Financial Institutions Desk
paras: Vantara Seguros has asked us to review the group structure before the end of the quarter. The board has already decided to move the reinsurance arm out of the current holding, and it has agreed to fund the operation this year. What the board has not decided is the route. Two of the three options involve interposing a new entity between the Brazilian parent and the offshore arm, and one of them risks losing the treaty benefit the group has relied on since 2021.

We recommend interposing a holding entity in a treaty jurisdiction and consolidating the three insurance vehicles into it. This route avoids triggering the new withholding obligation, and it keeps the group inside the exposure ceiling agreed with the board in March. We do not recommend the second route. It offers better tax optimization on paper, but the group would risk losing its legal standing before the authority if the structure were ever challenged, and no client should try defending a position it cannot document.

One point deserves attention. The board wanted to opt out of the special regime in order to simplify reporting, and last year somebody suggested doing that before the restructuring. We advise the group not to. If it opts out first, it will not manage to secure the ruling in time, and the only remaining route would be to file for an appeal after the assessment. What is at stake is not the rate: it is eighteen months of delay. Please remember to confirm with the tax director that the group has stopped filing under the old regime, because the December return cannot be amended twice.
reading.source: Internal client briefing -- ALMA financial institutions desk (adapted for class)
